# keel

> keel turns coding agents into work owners. It is a project-neutral, multi-agent
> workflow backbone that drives a GitHub issue from intake to done: select →
> branch → implement → CI → review → test → merge → capture → close. Projects set
> their values in `project.yaml` and snap their own logic into named extension
> slots. Stdlib-first Python CLI, single runtime dependency, 100% test coverage,
> 17 `/keel` commands. Installs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor (partial) and
> Antigravity; delegates work to hosted models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), any OpenAI-compatible
> API, or an agent CLI.

## Docs

- [Home](https://keel-ship.dev/): overview, positioning, and quick start
- [Documentation](https://keel-ship.dev/docs.html): commands, config, extension slots, and the fixed backbone
- [Coverage report](https://keel-ship.dev/coverage.html): test-coverage dashboard, generated from the coverage run each time the site is built

## Articles

- [A squash merge silently reverted our release — and CI stayed green](https://keel-ship.dev/silent-revert.html): a stale branch overwrote a published release while every test passed, and the timing check that catches it
- [Long unattended agent runs: where keel stops them, and why](https://keel-ship.dev/long-runs.html): six practices for long agent runs, what keel does for each, and a real run it stopped at the merge with the missing evidence named
- [100% coverage didn't prove our fixes were tested](https://keel-ship.dev/revert-check.html): coverage says every line ran, not that a test fails when a fix is undone; keel's opt-in revert-check gate reverts each change alone, a real run of it, and what it does not check

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/berkayturanci/keel): source, issues, and releases

## Key concepts

- Fixed backbone: the invariant step sequence every issue flows through
- Project-neutral core: all project specifics live in `project.yaml`, read via the `keel` CLI
- Extension slots: named hooks where a project snaps in its own implementers/reviewers
- Auditable evidence chain: commit-SHA-bound review provenance, model attribution, and explicit operator deferrals
- Test-first mode: `knobs.implement_mode: tdd` writes the failing tests first, and the blocking `tdd-order` gate verifies that order
- Gate-verified iteration: `knobs.loop` repeats the implementation until the command gates pass, at most `max_iterations` times (a red run after that blocks the issue); under test-first mode it wraps the implementation phase only
- Learning chain: with `learning.enabled`, `learning.mode: create-learning` and a sink, an applied capture writes a Markdown lesson — committed onto the pull request by `keel capture-land` when the sink is inside the repository, written after the merge when it is not — and later implement and review briefs read matching lessons back
- Pure-core / thin-I/O split with a strict 100% coverage bar
